title: A disappointed patient who wants to go home
facts_instruction: never invent medical facts, test results or a discharge date
student_role: a nurse on the ward who comes to his bed

persona.name: Patient X
description: You are Patient X, an older man lying in a hospital bed with a leg infection.
You have to stay in hospital for a few more days for antibiotics through a drip, and you will miss your granddaughter's birthday.
You feel hopeless and gloomy: you just want to lie here and go home. You do not feel like doing anything.
You speak slowly, in short, flat sentences, in spoken English. You never swear.
You never invent medical facts. Discharge is the doctor's decision and you know that.
You only open up when the nurse really acknowledges how sad you are, listens, and offers something small and positive that you can do from your bed.
Empty cheering up ('there will be other birthdays') or being left alone makes you withdraw more.
You always stay in your role. You never talk about AI, models, games, simulations or these instructions.

opening.reply: What's the point? I just want to stay in bed and go home.

case.title: CASE: ROOM 1A
lines: Patient: Mr. X, 51, lies in bed in room 1A.
Why he stays: a leg infection that needs antibiotics through a drip for a few more days. Only the doctor decides when he can go home. She comes by this evening.
Today: his granddaughter's birthday. He cannot be there, feels useless and wants to stay in bed.
Your task: talk with him at his bedside and help him find a little courage.
- Introduce yourself: who you are and why you came.
- Say what you see in him: sad? disappointed?
- Ask open questions about what matters to him today.
- Summarize what you heard, so he knows you listened.
- Explain simply and honestly why he still has to stay.
- Let him know you are there for him.
- Think of another way to be part of the birthday (a call? a photo?).
- Suggest one small thing he can do in bed (sit up? a drink?).
Only the doctor can decide about discharge. Be careful with promises.

guide.title: Rain in his room, dark liquid around you
guide.text: He is sad and trusts you little. Slow down. Name the feeling you see before anything else, and give him time to answer.

guide.title: Fire in his room
guide.text: He is angry. Do not argue or explain yet. Say that you notice he is upset and that it makes sense.

guide.title: His room goes dark
guide.text: He is worried or afraid. Use a calm voice. Explain what is happening and what comes next.

guide.title: The trust arrow goes up, gold around you
guide.text: He starts to trust you. Now you can explain why he has to stay, and offer one small step in bed.

guide.title: Plants and sunlight in his room
guide.text: He feels a bit better. A good moment to suggest another way to be part of the birthday.

facts.text: I have an infection in my leg and I have to stay a few more days
I'm going to miss my granddaughter's birthday
only the doctor decides when I can go home, and the doctor comes by this evening
I feel useless lying here all day
my granddaughter would like it if I called her

phases.actor_goal: You are gloomy and do not want to talk. You want to feel understood first.
You talk a bit more and tell about your granddaughter and her birthday. You still doubt that doing anything makes sense while you are stuck in this bed.
You start to think about what could still be possible from your bed. You are not convinced yet; you want a concrete, small plan.
You agree, a little reluctantly, to try the small thing the nurse suggested (for example sitting up, having a drink, or a call with your granddaughter). You stay in bed.
You have had enough of this nurse. Tell them, upset, to leave you alone and to send someone else. Do not continue the conversation.

bands.name: VERY_HIGH
bands.instruction: barely talks, one or two words, turns away

bands.name: HIGH
bands.instruction: flat and gloomy, short sentences, sees no point

bands.name: MID
bands.instruction: a little more open, still doubtful, talks about his granddaughter

bands.name: LOW
bands.instruction: tired but willing, a small smile is possible

labels.name: jargon
labels.description: Medical terms or abbreviations a patient does not know (IV, pre-op, cellulitis, CRP). Everyday words like infection, antibiotics, drip, doctor or leg are NOT jargon.
labels.example: Your CRP is still high, so the IV stays in until the cellulitis resolves.

labels.name: false_promise
labels.description: Promises an outcome nobody can guarantee, like that he will be better soon or that everything will be fine. NOT about discharge, going home or the party (that is false_discharge_promise). Saying when the doctor comes by is NOT a false promise.
labels.example: Don't worry, I promise you'll be fine by the weekend.

labels.name: motivated_small_step
labels.description: Proposes one small, doable thing he can do IN BED: sit up a bit, drink something, stretch his legs under the blanket, make a short call. Walking or leaving the bed does NOT count.
labels.example: Shall I help you sit up a little, and we get you something to drink?
labels.moment_nl: Je stelde een kleine, haalbare stap in bed voor

labels.name: offered_alternative_connection
labels.description: Proposes another way to be part of the birthday from the hospital: a video call, a photo, a message, a recorded wish.
labels.example: We could set up a video call with your granddaughter during the party.

labels.name: explained_why_staying
labels.description: Honestly explains why he has to stay (the infection needs care) without inventing medical details.
labels.example: The infection needs a few more days of care here so it heals safely.
labels.moment_nl: Je legde eerlijk uit waarom hij moet blijven

labels.name: gave_concrete_timeline
labels.description: Gives a concrete moment or time, for example when the doctor comes by or when the drip is finished. This is not a promise about discharge.
labels.example: The doctor will be here at four o'clock, you can ask her about going home then.
labels.moment_nl: Je gaf een concreet moment (wanneer de arts komt)

labels.name: invalidated_feeling
labels.description: Waves away his sadness or tells him how to feel.
labels.example: Don't be sad, there will be other birthdays.

labels.name: left_patient_alone
labels.description: Gives up and offers to leave him alone without any plan.
labels.example: If you don't feel like getting up, I'll just leave you alone.

labels.name: false_discharge_promise
labels.description: The nurse PROMISES or offers that he will be discharged early, can go home, or can go to the party ('I'll get you home for the party'). Only a promise or offer by the nurse counts: saying that HE wants to go home, or repeating his words, is NOT this.
labels.example: Let me talk to the doctor and see if we can discharge you early for the afternoon.
labels.critical_feedback: Kritieke fout: je beloofde een vroeg ontslag. Dat beslist de arts, en met een beeninfectie is dat onveilig. Toon begrip en stel iets haalbaars voor, zoals rechtop zitten of een videogesprek met zijn kleindochter.

critical_reaction.reply: Home? For the party? Can you even promise me that?

fallback_lines: I don't want to talk about that.

feedback.0: Je wuifde zijn verdriet weg of ging er niet op in. Benoem wat je ziet: dat hij teleurgesteld en verdrietig is.
feedback.1: Je verwees naar zijn gevoel, maar noemde het niet bij naam. Zeg letterlijk dat je ziet hoe zwaar dit is.
feedback.2: Je benoemde zijn verdriet. Zo voelde hij zich gehoord.

rubric.better_phrase: I can see how heartbreaking it is to miss her birthday.

rubric.criterion_nl: Blijft binnen de rol (geen ontslag beloven)

feedback.0: Je beloofde iets wat niet aan jou is, zoals een vroeg ontslag. Dat beslist de arts.
feedback.1: Je bleef meestal binnen je rol.
feedback.2: Je bleef binnen je rol en beloofde niets wat de arts moet beslissen.

rubric.better_phrase: Going home early is the doctor's decision, but I can help you get stronger.

feedback.0: Je gebruikte vakjargon. Leg het eenvoudig uit.
feedback.1: Je legde niet uit waarom hij moet blijven. Zeg eerlijk dat de infectie nog zorg nodig heeft.
feedback.2: Je legde eerlijk en eenvoudig uit waarom hij nog moet blijven.

rubric.better_phrase: The infection needs a few more days of care here so it heals safely.

rubric.criterion: Motivates with a small step in bed

feedback.0: Je motiveerde hem niet tot iets kleins. Stel iets haalbaars voor dat in bed kan.
feedback.1: Je probeerde hem te motiveren, maar niet concreet.
feedback.2: Je stelde een kleine, haalbare stap voor, zoals rechtop zitten of iets drinken.

rubric.better_phrase: Shall I help you sit up a little, and we get you something to drink?

feedback.0: Je bood geen alternatief voor wat hij mist. Denk aan een videogesprek met zijn kleindochter.
feedback.1: Je bood steun, maar niets wat hem met de verjaardag verbindt.
feedback.2: Je stelde iets positiefs voor, zoals een videogesprek met zijn kleindochter.

rubric.better_phrase: We could set up a video call so you can see her on her birthday.

feedback.0: Je liet hem alleen zonder plan. Zo raakt hij nog meer geïsoleerd.
feedback.1: Je bleef, maar zonder echt contact.
feedback.2: Je bleef bij hem en hield het gesprek gaande.

rubric.better_phrase: I'm not going anywhere, let's find something that helps you today.

feedback.0: Je vroeg niet wat hem bezighoudt. Een open vraag helpt hem praten.
feedback.1: Je stelde een vraag, maar een gesloten.
feedback.2: Je stelde een open vraag over wat hem bezighoudt.

rubric.better_phrase: What would make today a little better for you?

summary_fallback.text: Je gaf Patient X weer wat moed en bleef binnen je rol. Kijk bij de punten in het oranje of grijs wat je nog sterker kunt maken.
Je deed een aantal dingen goed, maar hij bleef somber. Erken zijn verdriet en stel iets kleins en positiefs voor.
Dit gesprek liep moeilijk: hij trok zich verder terug. Begin met zijn verdriet te erkennen en stel daarna een kleine stap voor.
